APPROVAL OF MINUTES
  EL MONTE CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING
  OF AUGUST 15, 2023

MEETING JOINTLY AND REGULARLY WITH THE EL MONTE HOUSING AUTHORITY; EL
MONTE PUBLIC FINANCING AUTHORITY; EL MONTE WATER AUTHORITY; EL MONTE
PARKING AUTHORITY; SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE FORMER EL MONTE COMMUNITY
REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY; HOUSING SUCCESSOR AGENCY; AND, FROM TIME TO
TIME, SUCH OTHER BODIES OF THE CITY WHOSE MEMBERSHIP IS COMPOSED
EXCLUSIVELY OF THE MEMBERSHIP OF THE CITY COUNCIL

1.  CALL TO ORDER: 6:02 p.m.

2.  ROLL CALL FOR CITY COUNCIL AND AUTHORITY BODIES:

  Jessica Ancona, Mayor/Chair – present
  Martin Herrera, Mayor Pro Tem/Authority Member – present
  Marisol Cortez, Councilmember/Authority Member – present
  Victoria Martinez Muela, Councilmember/Authority Member – present
  Alma D. Puente, Councilmember/Authority Member – present
  Richard Rojo, Councilmember/Authority Member – present
  Dr. Julia Ruedas, Councilmember/Authority Member – present

3.  APPROVAL OF AGENDA:

  m) Councilmember Puente
  s) Councilmember Rojo  7-0

4.  CLOSED SESSION:

  The City Council and the various legislative bodies whose membership is composed
  exclusively of the membership of the City Council will attempt to address and complete all
  Closed Session business between 6:00 p.m. and 7:00 p.m. If the City Council completes
  all Closed Session business prior to 7:00 p.m., the City Council will take a short recess
  and commence all Open Session proceedings promptly at 7:00 p.m. In the event the City
  Council is unable to address or complete all agendized Closed Session items by 7:00
  p.m., the City Council will hear all such remaining items toward the end of the meeting,
  immediately following Council Communications. Should any member of the public wish to
  address the City Council on any agendized Closed Session matter, the City Council shall
  allow such person to address the City Council on such matter(s) prior to going into Closed
  Session, provided that all persons wishing to address the Council on an agendized Closed
  Session matter shall (i) call-in or submit a speaker card in the manner prescribed on page
  1 of this agenda, above, prior to the City Council going into closed session; and (ii) be
  subject to a single speaker time allotment of three (3) continuous minutes total per
  speaker to address the City Council on any or all closed session items of business.

  Mayor Ancona invited members of the public to address the City Council on Closed
  Session Item 4.1.

  Mayor Ancona and the City Council recessed into Closed Session at approximately
  6:03 p.m. Mayor Ancona and the City Council reconvened from Closed Session at
  approximately 7:03 p.m.

  Assistant City Attorney reported out of Closed Session with respect to Item 4.1.

8.  GENERAL PUBLIC COMMENT:

  This time has been set aside for members of the public to directly address the City Council
  on agendized items of business (other than those agendized as public hearing or closed
  session items) or on any other matter of interest to the speaker/caller that is within the
  subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council, the Housing Authority, the Financing
  Authority and/or the Water Authority (collectively, the “Council”). Each speaker/caller will
  be limited to a single allotment of three (3) continuous minutes total to address the Council
  on any or all matters covered by this section. As explained more specifically under the
  Public Hearing portion of this agenda, members of the public wishing to offer comment on
  items of business agendized under the Public Hearing portion of the agenda shall have a
  separate allotment of three (3) continuous minutes per speaker per public hearing item.
  Except as otherwise provided under the Brown Act (Gov. Code Section 54950 et seq.),
  the Council may not deliberate or take action upon any matter not listed on this posted
  agenda but may order that any such matter be placed on the agenda for a subsequent
  meeting. The Council may also direct staff to investigate certain matters for consideration
  at a future meeting. Persons wishing to address the Council on matters covered under
  General Public Comment shall call in or submit a speaker card in the manner prescribed
  on page 1 of this agenda, above, by or before the General Public Comment portion of the
  agenda is closed. The City Council shall be under no obligation to entertain comments
  from speakers/callers who submit cards or call in to speak on matters covered by the
  section after the General Public Comment portion of the agenda is closed.

   City Council Meeting Minutes of August 15, 2023

  Jose Salazar – Spoke about the incident that took place on September 17, 2022.

  Francisco Rivera – Spoke about an incident that took place on June 28, 2023.

  Kenneth MacKenzie – Spoke about city officials and city employees who are a liability to
  the City must be asked to resign by the City.

  Julio Ramirez – Spoke about Farmer’s Market, Main Street, and the Fireworks Committee.

  Jane Myring – Was at the meeting to follow-up on the City’s Policy for the use by non-
  profit of City facilities.

  Mary Ann Powers – Spoke about a San Gabriel Valley Tribune article from July 26, 2023.
  Spoke about the City Manager.
  Eduardo Sauceda – Spoke about the MacClaren Hall Project and other issues at the City.
  Cosme Jimenez – Spoke about City Councilmembers and the City Manager.

  Tony Garcia – Thanked the City Council for the support with the street vendors and asked
  that the City Council not allow food trucks in the City.

  Sandra Meza – Spoke about her concerns relating to the issuance of permits by the City
  to food trucks.

  Humberto Navarro – Requested that the City Council not allow food trucks in the City.

  Gabriel Ramirez – Would like to have the City Council meeting adjourned in memory of
  his friend Albert Bashir. Also spoke about Main Street.

18.  COUNCIL COMMUNICATIONS/REPRTS:

  18A.  Mayor Ancona

  Mayor Ancona informed the City Council that she had an opportunity to visit the
  complete streets area at the Farmer’s Market during Night Out and was happy to
  see that the City is providing good outreach to support this program.

  7
   City Council Meeting Minutes of August 15, 2023

  Thanked Parks & Recreation staff for the summer program being offered.

  Music on Main is on August 31st kicking off Hispanic Heritage Month.

  Mark your calendars State of the City Saturday, September 9th at 9:00 am.

  18A.1 Update and Discussion on the Chamber of Commerce Contract.

  The City Attorney’s Office is working on the Chamber of Commerce
  Contract. Would like to see them come back as a resource.

  Councilmember Martinez Muela did advise that the Chamber of Commerce
  does have a contract with South El Monte and maybe the City of El Monte
  can use that agreement as a template to move this item forward.

  Mayor Pro Tem Herrera advised that there was a contract a few years ago
  and would like to see a scope of work for this contract.

  18A.2 Discussion on Naming of Merced Linear Park.

  Is there an update regarding the naming of Merced Linear Park.

  Councilmember Martinez Muela informed the City Council the Parks Ad
  Hoc had a discussion regarding this. There has been discussion regarding
  this. There is a deadline regarding a decision on this.

  Mayor Pro Tem Herrera would like to see what the community’s feedback
  is regarding the naming of Merced Linear Park.

18B.  Mayor Pro Tem Herrera

  Mayor Pro Tem Herrera also requested a policy regarding abatement of vacant
  lots.

  Mayor Ancona requested that the policy not only address vacant lots but unkept
  properties.

  Neighborhood Services Manager JD Whitaker informed the City Council that he is
  working on this and will be providing the City Council with a memo regarding this.

18C.  Councilwoman Cortez

  18C.1 Discussion Regarding a Policy to Abate and Maintain Vacant Properties.

  Thanked the City Manager and staff for the clean-up of the RV property on
  Valley. Would like to have a policy regarding the process for clean-up of
  vacant properties.

  18C.2 Update Regarding Unhoused Encampment Under the 605 Freeway Bridge
  on Valley Boulevard.

  Concerned about the increased amount of unhoused encampments it is
  getting closer to the City of El Monte. There is a vacant lot on Valley and
  Durfee would like to know if there is something the City can do.

  Mayor Ancona – Is that Caltrans?

  City Manager Alma Martinez will be reaching out to the City of Industry
  regarding this matter.

  Mayor Pro Tem made a recommendation to reach out to the County to
  address this matter and provide homeless outreach.

  8
   City Council Meeting Minutes of August 15, 2023

  18C.3 Update Regarding a Citywide Economic Development Plan.

  City Manager Alma Martinez provided an update regarding an RFP that is
  being prepared for this.

  Mayor will follow up with staff regarding a Development Ad Hoc meeting.

18D.  Councilwoman Martinez Muela

  18D.1 Status Update on Coordinating Council Upcoming Meeting and Flyer.

  Shared information with the City Council regarding the Coordinating
  Council. Invited the Council to come out and enjoy the Coordinating
  Council.

  Mayor Ancona is glad to see this back and wanted to make sure that the
  City Council is okay with Councilmember Martinez Muela taking the reins
  back of the Coordinating Council.

  Councilmember Martinez Muela thanked staff and the City Council for their
  support and work on the Back-to-School Resources Fair.

18E.  Councilwoman Puente

  18E.1 Discussion Regarding Parking Permits in the City.

  Discussed the impact of the multi-unit complexes in the City wanted to
  inquire if there is an interest in having staff prepare a presentation
  regarding bringing parking permits to the City.

  Mayor Ancona agreed with this and would like to see what other cities are
  doing.

  Mayor Pro Tem Herrera made the same request.

  Councilmember Martinez Muela informed the City Council that this has
  been on the Council’s agenda for some time now. Requesting information
  from staff regarding this matter.

  Neighborhood Services Manager JD Whitaker provided the City Council an
  update informing the City Council that he has been working with the Public
  Works Director regarding this. They will be bringing something to the City
  Council in an upcoming meeting.

18F.  Councilman Rojo

  18F.1 Update Regarding Meeting with the Operations Manager from End
  Overdose.

  Councilmember Rojo provided an update regarding his meeting with
  Anthony Banuelos from End Overdose.

  Mayor Pro Tem Herrera informed that the Los Angeles Public Health is
  disbursing doses of Narcan at community events.

  Mayor Ancona asked the Chief if the Police Department is equipped with
  doses of Narcan.

  Chief Fisher advised the City Council that the Police Department does have
  Narcan doses.

  9
   City Council Meeting Minutes of August 15, 2023

  18G.  Councilwoman Dr. Ruedas

  18G.1 Discussion Regarding Promoting Summaries of City Council Meetings, and
  Upcoming Public Meetings.

  Would like to see some promoting and bringing recaps to the public
  regarding the City’s public meetings.  Commended the City’s
  Communication/Graphic Designer regarding his work on what he does.

  18G.2 Update Regarding Qualifications for the Planning Commission.

  Requested update regarding the qualification for the Planning Commission.
  Staff will be bringing some options regarding this. Has research been done
  regarding what other jurisdictions have regarding qualifications for the
  planning commission.

  City Manager Alma Martinez informed the City Council that staff is working
  on this item and will bring back information to the City Council.

  Mayor Ancona would like to see staff work on this so that we can eliminate
  some hurdles in appointing members of the community to the Planning
  Commission.

  Mayor Pro Tem Herrera recommended that some type of training be made
  available to those individuals who are appointed to the Planning
  Commission and other Commissions/Committees.

19.  ADJOURNMENT:
